_comment: Skeleton of a 12-slide research talk (recipe in references/presentations.md). Every [bracket] is yours to replace; the chart uses example data and says so (EXAMPLE FIGURE) until real results replace it. Draft build: python3 scripts/new_deck.py scripts/examples/decks/research-talk-skeleton.json -o out/talk-draft.pptx --allow-placeholders --render. The final build must pass without --allow-placeholders.
title: [Talk title]
author: [Presenter Name]

slides.title: [Talk title: the finding]
slides.subtitle: [One line on the contribution]
slides.notes: Say the finding in the first minute. Venue and date in AP style, all caps (SEPT. 23, 2026).

slides.title: Agenda
slides.notes: The five items are the section numbers every eyebrow and divider reuses ("section": N in the spec). Delete the timing fields for an untimed talk.

slides.subtitle: [Why this problem matters, in one line]

slides.title: [The problem in one sentence]
body: [Who has the problem and what it costs them]
slides.notes: No figure slot filled here, so new_deck deletes it. Add "figure" with a real photo or plot (and "figure_alt") when you have one.

slides.title: [Result as a sentence]

chart.alt: Bar chart of example data, not results: mean seconds per task for the baseline (80), condition A (70), condition B (55) and the proposed method (45), which is highlighted.

slides.label: [what the number means, compared with what]
slides.notes: Replace the example values with the real data, the flag with the source, and update the alt text with the real takeaway and numbers.

slides.statement: [The one sentence you want the audience to repeat.]

slides.title: Plan and status
slides.notes: Status is a glyph plus a word plus a color (complete, on-track, at-risk, late, not-started), so nothing depends on color alone. Six body rows at most.

slides.title: References
references: [1]	[Author, A. and Author, B.] [Title of the paper]. In [Proceedings], [year]. [DOI]

slides.title: Acknowledgements and funding
slides.text: This work was supported by [Sponsor] under [Grant No.]. We thank [collaborators] for [contribution].
slides.notes: Only real sponsors and award numbers, confirmed by the PI. Put each sponsor-supplied logo in logo1-logo4 (with "logo1_alt" and so on): the four panels are fixed on the layout, so with fewer sponsors move this to an ATR - Title + Content slide. NSF-funded work adds the disclaimer and the NSF full-color logo (0.625 in or larger).
